greek: Ἤκουσεν δὲ Ιοθορ ὁ ἱερεὺς Μαδιαμ ὁ γαμβρὸς Μωυσῆ πάντα, ὅσα ἐποίησεν κύριος Ισραηλ τῷ ἑαυτοῦ λαῷ· ἐξήγαγεν γὰρ κύριος τὸν Ισραηλ ἐξ Αἰγύπτου.
hint: Jethro, priest of Midian and Moses' father-in-law, hears all the lord has done for Israel in bringing them out of Egypt.

notes.text: γαμβρός, Middle Liddell's any one connected by marriage, then a son-in-law, a father-in-law, for the Hebrew ḥōtēn.
To his own people, the reflexive between the article and its noun, read after the noun.

(Μωυσῆς, from Hebrew Mōšeh, which the Hebrew of 2:10 hears in māšâ, "to draw out")
(Ισραηλ, from Hebrew Yiśrāʾēl, which the Hebrew of Genesis 32:29 hears in śārâ ʿim ʾĕlōhîm, "he strove with God")
(Αἴγυπτος, the Greek name of the land; Hebrew Miṣrayim)

hint: With her come her two sons; one is named Gershom, for Moses said he was a sojourner in a foreign land.

notes.text: I was, the imperfect of εἰμί, which the formula for ἦν does not take: it is the first person.
